figures.caption: Table 1: Approximation results for the functions α1, . . . , α4, including both smooth and singular cases. For each ε, the table reports the network architecture (L,W ), the total complexity Ctot. The approximation errors are given in terms of infinity norm (Maxα) and mean squared error (MSEα), HP-spline reconstruction errors are computed using uniformly spaced knots with step size 0.1, and are reported for both predicted and nominal parameters. The propagation error measures the discrepancy between the corresponding reconstructed signals, quantifying the effect of approximating α.

Figure 1: Comparison between the empirical generalization gap (GenGap) and the theoretical boundD/ √ n as a function of the sample size n, for different values of the parameter A ∈ {0.5, 1, 5.5, 10}. Each panel shows how the empirical gap relates to its corresponding bound as n increases.
Figure 2: Comparison between the empirical generalization gap GenGapJ and corresponding theoretical bound Dj/ √ n as functions of the sample size n, for J ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} and A = 1.

Figure 3: Comparison of HP-spline regression performance using predicted and optimal α across three scenarios. Solid and dashed lines represent the two methods, while horizontal dotted lines indicate their corresponding mean values. Results are reported in terms of MSE and RE on a logarithmic scale, computed for each individual test data instance using neural network-based predictions of α. HP-spline reconstruction errors are evaluated on the corresponding test signals using uniformly spaced knots with step size 0.1.
